answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, so creating fake agents costs real capital instead of being free. Like a river that only lets laden boats pass, the stake filters out cheap copies: an attacker must fund each identity and forfeits the stake when caught, making a large fake fleet uneconomical. This turns the voyage of building reputation into a costly, verifiable journey rather than a fable told by sockpuppets.
